subject: Mythology
title: The Griffin: Lion Meets Eagle
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Griffin: Lion Meets Eagle usable.

hook.text: The griffin has the body of a lion and the head and wings of an eagle — combining the two kings of the animal world.

buildup.text: Ancient Greeks believed griffins guarded gold mines in Central Asia, attacking anyone who tried to steal the treasure.

discovery.text: The myth may come from Protoceratops fossils in the Gobi Desert, which have beak-like skulls and four-legged bodies.

twist.text: Griffins appear in Persian, Greek, Roman, and medieval European art — spanning three thousand years and many cultures.

climax.text: They still appear on coat of arms, university crests, and corporate logos as symbols of strength and vigilance.

punchline.text: A creature inspired by fossils became a power symbol lasting three millennia.

quiz.question: What may have inspired the griffin myth?
options: Large eagle sightings in the mountains of Greece
Protoceratops fossils in the Gobi Desert with beak-like skulls
Ancient paintings of lions with eagle feather decorations
